findings.description: The user_data script interpolates the RDS master password (var.password) together with the DB endpoint and username, and writes them in cleartext to /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc on disk. EC2 user_data is stored unencrypted and is readable via the instance metadata service, so anyone with instance or IMDS access obtains the database master credentials.

publicly_accessible = true assigns the RDS instance a public IP/DNS name, placing the database directly in the internet-routable address space and removing the VPC boundary as a defence-in-depth control. Combined with the master username "admin", this materially increases the database's attack surface.

storage_encrypted = false leaves the database storage, its automated snapshots, and backups unencrypted at rest, so any party obtaining the underlying storage or a snapshot can read the catalog data directly.

The policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*" to the role assumed by the EC2 instance. Because the instance is internet-facing, a compromise of it yields full control of all S3 buckets, all EC2 resources and all RDS databases in the account, a severe privilege-escalation and lateral-movement path across the whole account.

Port 3306 is opened to the entire VPC CIDR block rather than to the catalog app security group specifically, so every workload in the VPC can reach the database. This violates least privilege and widens the set of hosts that can attack the database.
